chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi 'Abdullah, from one of his companions, raising it, said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who cultivates enmity will reap what he sowed.'

key_terms.الْعَدَاوَة: Enmity, hostility, or animosity between people
key_terms.حَصَدَ: To reap, harvest, or receive the consequence
key_terms.زَرَعَ: To sow, cultivate, or plant (metaphorically for initiating an action)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'whoever sows enmity will reap it' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates the principle of reciprocal justice in social dynamics, asserting that the enmity one sows will inevitably be harvested in kind. This maxim, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the causal link between interpersonal conduct and divine retribution, serving as a practical guide for maintaining harmony within the Shia community. It reflects the broader Shia emphasis on *adl* (justice) extending from individual actions to communal relationships.
